title: Writing into an array like it is memory
snippet:
import jax.numpy as jnp

x = jnp.zeros(3)
x[0] = 1.0  # NumPy habit: update the array in place
error: TypeError: JAX arrays are immutable and do not support in-place item assignment. Instead of x[idx] = y, use x = x.at[idx].set(y) or another .at[] method: https://jax.readthedocs.io/en/latest/_autosummary/jax.numpy.ndarray.at.html
fix:
import jax.numpy as jnp

x = jnp.zeros(3)
x = x.at[0].set(1.0)  # a new array; under jit the copy is usually elided
why: Chapter 01's first invariant, met as an error message. A `jnp` array is a value, not a place, so there is nothing to write into. `.at[...].set` expresses the same intent as a pure function, and XLA reuses the old buffer when the old value is dead.

title: Branching on a value the trace cannot see
snippet:
import jax
import jax.numpy as jnp

@jax.jit
def f(x):
    if x.sum() > 0:  # the tracer has no value to branch on
        return x
    return -x

f(jnp.ones(3))
error:
TracerBoolConversionError: Attempted boolean conversion of traced array with shape bool[].
The error occurred while tracing the function f at <string>:5 for jit. This concrete value was not available in Python because it depends on the value of the argument x.
See https://jax.readthedocs.io/en/latest/errors.html#jax.errors.TracerBoolConversionError
why: Tracing runs your Python once with stand-ins that carry shape and dtype but no values, so a Python `if` on data has nothing to decide with. `lax.cond` stages both branches into the program and picks at run time, which is what you meant.

title: A boolean mask whose output shape depends on data
error:
NonConcreteBooleanIndexError: Array boolean indices must be concrete; got ShapedArray(bool[3])

See https://jax.readthedocs.io/en/latest/errors.html#jax.errors.NonConcreteBooleanIndexError
why: Shapes are fixed at trace time, and `x[x > 0]` has a length only the data knows. `jnp.where` keeps the shape and masks instead; when you truly need compaction, do it outside jit or with a static bound and padding.

title: Asking grad for the derivative of a vector
snippet:
import jax
import jax.numpy as jnp

g = jax.grad(lambda x: x * 2.0)(jnp.ones(3))
error: TypeError: Gradient only defined for scalar-output functions. Output had shape: (3,).
fix:
import jax
import jax.numpy as jnp

g = jax.grad(lambda x: jnp.sum(x * 2.0))(jnp.ones(3))
J = jax.jacrev(lambda x: x * 2.0)(jnp.ones(3))  # the full Jacobian, if that was the ask
why: Reverse mode pulls one cotangent backward, so `grad` is defined for scalar outputs. Reduce to a scalar if you meant a loss; ask `jacrev` or `jacfwd` if you meant the whole Jacobian, and pick by the Jacobian's aspect ratio.

title: vmap told to batch an argument that has no batch axis
snippet:
import jax
import jax.numpy as jnp

def dot(a, b):
    return a @ b

a = jnp.ones((32, 8))
b = jnp.ones(8)
jax.vmap(dot)(a, b)  # default in_axes=0 tries to split b too
fix:
import jax
import jax.numpy as jnp

def dot(a, b):
    return a @ b

a = jnp.ones((32, 8))
b = jnp.ones(8)
out = jax.vmap(dot, in_axes=(0, None))(a, b)  # b broadcast to every row
why: `in_axes` defaults to 0 for every argument, and `b` has no axis of size 32 to give. Say which arguments carry the batch (`0`) and which ride along whole (`None`); the error names the sizes it saw, and they disagree for a reason.

title: A static argument that cannot be a cache key
error:
ValueError: Non-hashable static arguments are not supported. An error occurred while trying to hash an object of type <class 'list'>, [0]. The error was:
TypeError: unhashable type: 'list'
why: A static argument becomes part of the compilation cache key, so it must hash. Lists do not; tuples do. The chapter 03 rule applies twice here: statics are baked into the key, and every distinct value compiles its own executable.
